Overview

This document defines the Permissions Matrix for the

title: Permissions Matrix Design
text:
document defines the Permissions Matrix for the Trading module, outlining which roles have access to specific actions within the system. The strategy enforces fine-grained control through role-based access both at the backend and UI level.

2. Enforcement Layer

To ensure these permissions are reliably enforced across the stack, the following layers are implemented:

a. Backend Enforcement – Express

title: Permissions Matrix Design
text:
the following layers are implemented:

a. Backend Enforcement – Express Middleware

  • All protected API routes include a role-based middleware to verify user role against allowed roles for the action.

  • Middleware example:

title: Permissions Matrix Design
text:
example:

CopyEdit

function authorizeRoles(...allowedRoles) { return (req, res, next) => { const userRole = req.user.role; if (!allowedRoles.includes(userRole)) { return res.status(403).json({ message: "Forbidden" }); } next(); }; }

title: Permissions Matrix Design
text:
{ return res.status(403).json({ message: "Forbidden" }); } next(); }; }

  • Usage:

CopyEdit

app.post('/submit-emir', authorizeRoles('Compliance', 'Admin'), submitEmirHandler);

b. Frontend Enforcement

title: Permissions Matrix Design
text:
'Admin'), submitEmirHandler);

b. Frontend Enforcement – RBAC Hook on UI

  • UI components and buttons are conditionally rendered based on the user's role.

  • A custom RBAC hook provides permissions dynamically to the React components.

title: Permissions Matrix Design
text:
to the React components.

CopyEdit

const { hasPermission } = useRBAC(); if (hasPermission("Submit EMIR Report")) { return <SubmitReportButton />; }

  • This prevents unauthorized users from even seeing restricted UI actions.

title: Permissions Matrix Design
text:
prevents unauthorized users from even seeing restricted UI actions.

Security Best Practices

  • All actions are double-checked at the backend to prevent privilege escalation via API manipulation.

  • Role and permissions are fetched during login and cached securely in memory/local state.

  • UI components fail gracefully and do not disclose permission logic in the client.

title: Permissions Matrix Design
text:
components fail gracefully and do not disclose permission logic in the client.

Future Enhancements

  • Permission groups with nested roles

  • Admin-configurable role matrix from UI

  • Audit logs for permission-based access failures

  • Integration with Identity Provider (IdP) for SSO-driven RBAC

text: Trade Upload Ingestion Flow

title: Trade Upload Ingestion Flow
text:
Overview

This document describes the Trade Upload Ingestion Flow implemented within the Regulatory Reporting (Trading) system. It supports uploading of trade files in multiple formats, captures essential metadata, and stores files securely for downstream processing.

1. Supported File Formats

The system currently supports the following trade file formats for ingestion:

  • .csv –

title: Trade Upload Ingestion Flow
text:
the following trade file formats for ingestion:

  • .csv – Comma-separated values format; most commonly used for bulk trade uploads

  • .json – Structured format, useful for programmatic data submission

  • .xml – Extensible Markup Language, used by some legacy systems and vendors

All formats must adhere to predefined schema templates to be accepted for processing.

title: Trade Upload Ingestion Flow
text:
formats must adhere to predefined schema templates to be accepted for processing.

2. Metadata Captured

During the file upload process, the following metadata is automatically captured for auditing and traceability:

  • filename – Original name of the uploaded file

  • uploaded_by – User ID or email of the uploader (retrieved from the active session)

  • timestamp

title: Trade Upload Ingestion Flow
text:
email of the uploader (retrieved from the active session)

  • timestamp – Server-side time of upload (in UTC), used for logging and versioning

    • This metadata is stored alongside the uploaded file reference and is used in validation, reporting, and rollback logic.

    3. Tech Stack & Architecture

    The ingestion flow is implemented using the following technology components:

    • Frontend:

title: Trade Upload Ingestion Flow
text:
flow is implemented using the following technology components:

  • Frontend: React

    • Provides a user-friendly drag-and-drop upload interface

    • Validates file type before upload

    • Shows progress bar and upload result (success/failure)

  • Backend: Express.js (Node.js)

    • Receives and validates uploaded files

    • Extracts metadata and stores it along with file

title: Trade Upload Ingestion Flow
text:
and validates uploaded files

  • Extracts metadata and stores it along with file reference

  • Handles error responses and file integrity checks

  • Storage:

    • Primary: AWS S3 – Secure cloud storage with versioning and encryption enabled

    • Alternative: Local File System (FS) – Used for non-production or isolated deployments

title: Trade Upload Ingestion Flow
text:
File System (FS) – Used for non-production or isolated deployments

Security & Validation

  • All uploads are restricted to authenticated users with proper roles.

  • Files are scanned for size limits, format compliance, and integrity before storage.

  • Audit logs are maintained for all upload attempts (success or failure).

Future

Future Enhancements

  • Schema validation for uploaded files with real-time error feedback

  • Integration with S3 event notifications to trigger processing pipelines

  • Support for zipped/multi-part uploads

  • Upload history with download and reprocess options

title: Session Token Strategy
text: Session Token Strategy

title: Session Token Strategy
text:
This document outlines the Session Token Strategy implemented for the Regulatory Reporting application. The strategy ensures secure and seamless user sessions using industry-standard JWT-based authentication combined with secure token refresh mechanisms.

1. Token Type

  • Access Token (JWT)

    • A short-lived token used to authenticate user actions and API requests.

    • Encoded with user identity, role,

title: Session Token Strategy
text:
to authenticate user actions and API requests.

  • Encoded with user identity, role, and expiry time.

  • Stored in memory or browser storage depending on the client architecture (not in cookies for XSS protection).

  • Refresh Token (Secure Cookie)

    • A long-lived token stored securely as an HTTP-only, Secure, and SameSite=Strict cookie.

    • Used to generate new

title: Session Token Strategy
text:
and SameSite=Strict cookie.

  • Used to generate new access tokens without requiring user re-login.

  • Never exposed to JavaScript.

    • 2. Idle Timeout

    • Duration: 15 minutes

      • If there is no user interaction or activity for 15 minutes, the session is considered idle and the access token becomes invalid.

      • Any request made after this period

title: Session Token Strategy
text:
idle and the access token becomes invalid.

  • Any request made after this period without a valid refresh will redirect the user to re-authenticate.

    • 3. Refresh Policy

    • Interval: Every 10 minutes

      • A silent background call refreshes the access token using the refresh token at regular 10-minute intervals, provided the session is still active.

      • Prevents token expiry

title: Session Token Strategy
text:
10-minute intervals, provided the session is still active.

  • Prevents token expiry during active sessions.

  • If the refresh token has expired or is invalid, the user is logged out and prompted to re-login.

    • Security Considerations

    • All tokens are transmitted over HTTPS only.

    • Refresh tokens are rotated and invalidated upon logout or suspected

title: Session Token Strategy
text:
tokens are rotated and invalidated upon logout or suspected breach.

  • Failed refresh attempts trigger an alert and immediate logout for security.

    • Future Enhancements (Optional)

    • Integration with OAuth 2.0 Authorization Server

    • Support for device-based token revocation

    • MFA-based refresh token issuance

    • Admin dashboard for session/token monitoring

Overview

This document outlines the Trade Feature Extraction and

title: Trade Feature Extraction & Normalization
text:
document outlines the Trade Feature Extraction and Normalization process used in the trading data pipeline. The goal is to standardize key trade fields across multiple formats and reporting sources to enable accurate downstream processing, validation, and reporting.

Contents

1. Standard Fields Extracted

The normalization process ensures that all uploaded trade records are mapped to a unified internal schema.

title: Trade Feature Extraction & Normalization
text:
process ensures that all uploaded trade records are mapped to a unified internal schema. The following standard fields are extracted from all supported input formats:

Field

Description

trade_id

Unique identifier of the

title: Trade Feature Extraction & Normalization
text:
identifier of the trade

trade_date

Trade execution date (ISO 8601 format preferred)

counterparty_id

Internal/external identifier of the counterparty

product_type

Type/category of the traded financial instrument

These fields are mandatory and normalized across different upload templates (EMIR, MiFID,

title: Trade Feature Extraction & Normalization
text:
fields are mandatory and normalized across different upload templates (EMIR, MiFID, internal).

2. Value Mappings

To ensure consistency across heterogeneous sources, common value mappings are applied:

  • Currency Standardization

    • All currency codes (e.g., USD, eur, gbp) are normalized to ISO 4217 format (e.g., USD, EUR,

title: Trade Feature Extraction & Normalization
text:
are normalized to ISO 4217 format (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP)

  • Direction Enum Normalization

    • Trade direction strings like buy, BUY, purchase are all mapped to the enum:

      • Buy

      • Sell

  • Date Format Conversion

    • Any custom or regional date

title: Trade Feature Extraction & Normalization
text:
Format Conversion

  • Any custom or regional date formats are parsed and converted to standard YYYY-MM-DD format using locale-aware parsing

  • Null/Empty Value Handling

    • Placeholder values like N/A, null, - are mapped to actual null values in the system

    • 3. Normalization Engine

    The normalization logic is

title: Trade Feature Extraction & Normalization
text:
/>
3. Normalization Engine

The normalization logic is applied immediately after upload and validation, before persisting to the data store.

  • Implementation:

    • Modular rules using regex, lookup tables, and transformation functions

  • Execution Mode:

    • Scheduled Task triggered

title: Trade Feature Extraction & Normalization

Mode:

  • Can also be run manually for reprocessing or migration

  • Error Handling:

This document outlines the versioning strategy for the trade

title: Trade Ingestion Versioning Strategy
text:
document outlines the versioning strategy for the trade ingestion process. It is designed to maintain historical accuracy, ensure traceability of changes, and support administrative rollback in case of incorrect or unintended uploads. Versioning is maintained at both the file and individual trade row level.

Contents

1. Versioning Tables

To ensure robust tracking and auditability, two key tables are used:

title: Trade Ingestion Versioning Strategy

To ensure robust tracking and auditability, two key tables are used:

Date and time of upload

status

Status of the file (e.g., processed,

text:
of the file (e.g., processed, failed)

Boolean to indicate if file was rolled back

b. trade_change_log — Row-Level Diff Tracking

2. Comparison UI

The system provides a user-friendly interface to compare changes made across different versions of a trade.

  • Trade Diff Table

    • For any selected trade_id, users can view a side-by-side diff:

      • Left panel shows Old Values

      • Right panel shows New

text:
panel shows Old Values

  • Right panel shows New Values

  • Modified fields are highlighted (e.g., yellow for updated fields)

  • Version Selector

  • Permissions

    • Available to all roles, but read-only for non-admin

3. Rollback Mechanism

Admins have the ability to revert changes introduced by a specific version of an uploaded file.
